quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You can only pass other vehicles in areas where passing is legal and safe.

questions.question: Your body can only remove alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause:

options.text: No problems as long as you stay under the speed limit.
No problems on a motorcycle like it would in a car.
No problems as long as no other vehicles are nearby.
You to drift into another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You to drift into another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may drift into another lane or go off the road. Always slow down for turns.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and driving.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still affect you even if you wait one hour. It may still impact your riding ability.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and overall wear. How shiny the tires are is not important.

questions.question: Which material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Always wear clothing that covers your legs and arms completely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: Always stay away from the left side.
Always stay away from the right side.
Always stay away from the center.
Use whatever position is safest for current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whatever position is safest for current conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position to always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you to:
questions.explanation: Extra space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: To be more visible to other drivers, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to help other drivers see you. Bright clothing increases your visibility day and night.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can cause you to move into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Usually keeps you in your lane.
Is okay because motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to move into another lane.
questions.explanation: Going too fast around a corner may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you start a turn or curve.

questions.question: Keep enough space between you and the vehicle ahead so you can:

options.text: See dangers and have time to react.
Encourage other drivers to cut in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: See dangers and have time to react.
questions.explanation: Good following distance gives you space to stop or move if the car ahead stops suddenly. This space also helps you see road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: The best lane position is the one that:

options.text: Lets you ride close behind other vehicles.
Makes other drivers able to see you.
Puts you in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes other drivers able to see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed. Choose a position that gives you the most space.

questions.question: Before getting on the motorcycle, check all of these except:
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves when riding.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day, so you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright colors when riding so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Not be worn during the day.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials, especially at night, to help other drivers see you. Bright clothes with reflective materials make you more visible.

questions.question: In general, the body removes almost ______ of alcohol per hour.
questions.explanation: The body can eliminate about one drink per hour on average.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen the best?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Can long-term exposure to wind noise cause harm?

options.text: Yes, it can cause hearing loss.
No, it is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: Which surface provides good traction for tires?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement provides the best traction for motorcycles.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Near the shoulder on the right side.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in a position where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually, this means riding in the center of the lane. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride alongside a car?

options.text: It can place you in the driver's blind spot.
It is only dangerous when the road is wet.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can place you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly beside another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle can block your escape route.

questions.question: What happens if your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt breaks, power to the rear wheel stops immediately.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is an advantage of wearing a brightly-colored helmet?

options.text: It can help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle?

options.text: Tell them to take less busy roads.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has drunk too much to ride. Do whatever you can to stop them, including taking their keys. Arrange another way for them to get home.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should a motorcycle rider be ready for?

options.text: A parked car suddenly pulling into traffic.
Other drivers seeing you and staying away.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car suddenly pulling into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space between your motorcycle and any hazards.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen in daylight, what should you do to be more visible?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen in daylight. Always wear brightly-colored clothing while riding, even during the day, to increase your visibility.

questions.question: When you ride, the best gear to wear is:
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. A DOT-approved helmet, face protection, eye protection, and protective clothing are best.

questions.question: A simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see is to:

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to the frame.
Ride with the headlight turned on.
Ride on the shoulder when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with the headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing. Keep your headlight on at all times. Use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used in curves.
Should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave. This is normal and not dangerous. Keep a steady speed and go straight. Zigzagging to fight the weave is dangerous.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Allows you to see clearly to the sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets let you see to the sides as needed for safe riding. They have labels showing the manufacturer's name, instructions, and safety standards they meet.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle rider check their mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch for hazards behind you.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Downshift one gear at a time. Ease out the clutch slowly between each shift.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Wearing a quality helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: Use your mirrors at a stopped intersection to:

options.text: See if parked cars are entering traffic.
Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
See if someone is turning behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
questions.explanation: At a stopped intersection, check your mirrors for cars approaching from behind. The drivers may not see you. Be ready to react.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should lean when you lean. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Why is it better to ride in a small group?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always be trying to catch up to the group.
It will be difficult to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages. Other vehicles can pass them safely. They are less likely to get separated by traffic or stop lights. Slower riders do not have to rush to catch up.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required only for riders with a license for less than two years.
Required only for riders under 18 years old.

questions.explanation: All motorcycle riders must wear helmets in New Jersey. You can be fined for not wearing a helmet.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take rest breaks at least every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that makes you and your motorcycle easy to see. Bright, reflective clothing helps other drivers spot you.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce crash injuries?
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate you faster.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need regular checking?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small mechanical problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: The correct body position on a motorcycle:

options.text: Lets you sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
Lets you sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips.
Makes you lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keeps your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips. This position lets you reach and operate the controls easily and comfortably.
